deck: Table Rock and Taneycomo, written like a fishing magazine — two waters, one week, nothing invented on the outdoor desk.

play.title: Fish the wind.
play.body: Fall bass set up where the shad get blown. A crankbait that bangs is better than a worm that sits.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

body: ## Hooked on Branson Low, clear water on Table Rock combined with Taneycomo's predictable generation rhythm (minimal overnight/early morning flows building through the day) continues to drive strong early-fall trout action. Stocked rainbows remain aggressive while bass on the main lake transition deeper.

Today's Play: Hit Taneycomo seams and current breaks during lighter morning flows with pink worms under a float, 1/16–1/8 oz micro jigs (brown, black, white, sculpin), or zebra midges. Switch to heavier weighted rigs and drift when generation ramps later. Always verify the schedule before wading.

## The Week Table Rock has held steady in the low 912 ft range all week (911.88–912.3 ft), sitting 3+ ft below full pool with mostly light overnight generation and stronger afternoon/evening pushes (peaks 2,500–8,000+ cfs). Clarity remains excellent on both waters. Taneycomo patterns consistent: low morning flows favor light-line and wading; afternoon ramps push trout behind structure in seams. Local reports through mid-September show solid 20–30+ trout trips on pink worms, jigs, and flies plus reliable bass on points and brush. Verify today's exact cfs and schedule locally — power demand shifts flows fast.

## In Season Early Fall Transition. Cooling air and moderating water temps have trout active all day. Newly stocked rainbows stay aggressive; browns increasing as fall progresses. Bass on Table Rock shifting from summer shallows to deeper points, creek arms, and offshore structure (20–40 ft). High clarity demands clean presentations; fish are fattening for winter.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~2,500 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater trophy trout fishery stays excellent with consistent stocking and cold releases from Table Rock. Generation dictates tactics: minimal/low flows overnight and mornings enable light-line drifting, wading, and indicator fishing; stronger current later calls for weighted rigs and drifting seams/structure. Stocked rainbows aggressive; browns showing more with fall.

Wade below the dam (stay well outside the 760-ft closed zone) in low periods with micro jigs, pink worms under a float, or small flies. Drift boats and dock anglers excel when moving — hold in current breaks with weighted setups. Slot limit applies upper sections (rainbows 12–20" protected; artificials/flies only dam to Fall Creek). Below US 65, trout permit required to possess. Mega worms, San Juan worms, hoppers, scuds, zebra midges, and pink/salmon jigs producing per September reports. High clarity — clean, natural presentations win. Black jigs strong after dark. Call 866-494-1993 for latest SWPA schedule.

## Why open this tomorrow Overnight cooling, any SWPA schedule shift, or upstream weather/rain could tighten the bite, change wading windows, clarity, or oxygen levels by morning. A stronger generation push or passing front frequently repositions fish. Check the gage and schedule again — the early-fall transition often sharpens daily.
